latest_release.body:
## 💥 Breaking changes

- Disallow mixed string \<=> numeric arithmetic in eager (#30071)

## 🚀 Performance improvements

- Limit the memory of buckets sorted ahead in the sort flush (#30297)
- Make file readers wait for spills while over the memory budget (#30296)
- Count unspilled frames in the memory estimate right away (#30295)
- Simplify more boolean expressions and drop redundant null checks (#30293)
- Wait for spills while over the out-of-core memory budget (#30294)
- Lower the default out-of-core prefetch fraction to 0.5 (#30292)
- Aggregate unique and n\_unique in the streaming group-by itself (#30281)
- Return freed memory to the OS right away while out-of-core data is spilled (#30280)
- Gather `List(Array)` and `Array` columns without per-row slices (#30278)
- Evaluate the streaming window node out of core (#30282)
- Avoid deep copies when building a DataFrame from flat dataclasses (#30275)
- Sort the window partitions by each order key instead of their row encoding (#30277)
- Scan the haystack for a single needle in `is_in` (#30276)
- Prefer fixed-width columns when only the row count is needed (#30274)
- Native gather for List arrays (#30019)
- Evaluate windows in filter predicates in the streaming window node (#30272)
- Don't busy-wait in RAYON.block\_on (#30259)
- Encode nested Parquet levels directly from the level buffers (#30251)
- Reduce memory of CSV scans on wide rows (#30165)
- Avoid quadratic JSON serialization of nested lists and maps (#30203)
- Skip the gather when exploding lists without nulls (#30234)
- Speed up writing nested Parquet columns (#30245)
- Don't keep whole parquet string dictionaries alive for a few selected rows (#30248)
- Set default spill compression level to 1 (#30237)
- Reuse zstd contexts in compression and avoid memcpys (#30233)
- Remove repeated and scalar ordering keys before the sort rewrites (#30231)
- Remove repeated keys from by's (#30095)
- Keep only one guessed unique key per join order leaf (#30191)
- Don't let extra join keys shrink an estimate once one key is unique (#30190)
- Reduce binary size of asof join with `by` keys (#30192)
- Reduce binary size of SQL visitors and parallel group-by collect (#30171)
- Push as-of join key filters to the right input (#30123)
- Drop null as-of right keys with a parallel filter before the join node (#30125)
- Keep as-of nearest join state small (#30126)
- Explode lists in group\_by aggregations without a per-group apply (#30020)
- Streaming OOC group-by with shuffles (#29911)
- Drop scalar ordering keys in the optimizer (#30063)
- Merge union inputs that scan files of the same kind into one multi-file scan (#30056)
- Use the streaming scalar window for std, var and combined reductions in `over` (#30066)
- Limit the bytes of local CSV and NDJSON files read at once in multi-file scans (#30055)
- Check the matched flag of join keys in the table entry before the bitset (#30067)
- Track matched build rows of all join tables in a bitset (#30050)
- Add dedicated list gather kernels (#30049)
- Emit unmatched build rows of single-key joins in row order (#30037)
- Use `TopK` for sorts sliced at a nonzero offset (#29989)
- Add constant folding for more datetime ops (#30016)
- Rewrite the sum of a column plus a literal to a sum and a count of the column (#30011)
- Push predicates through order-keeping columns (#30007)
- Fix dead early exit in `coalesce` (#30013)
- Count distinct non-null values in SQL with one group-by in the streaming engine (#30009)
- Skip parquet row groups with the running top-k threshold (#30006)
- Keep decompressed plain string pages as the string data buffer (#29984)
- Fix some in-memory filter regressions (#29988)
- Decompress snappy and zstd parquet pages without zeroing the buffer (#29980)
- Speed up `str.len_chars` (#29972)
- Speed up `str.replace` for patterns that end in `.*$` (#29971)
- Use the Parquet string prefilter for literal `str.contains` and SQL `LIKE` (#29953)
- Keep single-chunk output when filtering wide

## Polars: Extremely fast Query Engine for DataFrames and SQL Polars is an analytical query engine written in Rust. Write your queries with the DataFrame API, in SQL, or mix both: they run through the same optimizer and the same engine. It is designed to be fast, easy to use and expressive. Key features are: - **Fast**: written from the ground up in Rust with multi-threaded, vectorized (SIMD) execution - **Spill to disk**: Operations that exceed available RAM can spill to disk - **Expressive API**: compose complex queries with powerful expressions - **Extensible**: extend Polars natively with custom code through [I/O and Expression plugins](https://docs.pola.rs/user-guide/plugins/) - **GPU support**: optionally accelerate queries on NVIDIA GPUs - **Interoperable**: uses the [Apache Arrow Columnar Format](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/Columnar.html) for zero-copy data sharing To learn more, read the [user guide](https://docs.pola.rs/). ## Polars in action ### DataFrame API Queries are composed from expressions or SQL.
